subject: Post-demo: data residency checklist & narrow-scope DPA questions
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Eliza Moreno <eliza.moreno@healthsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: data residency checklist & narrow-scope DPA questions

Hi Eliza — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and a handful of clarifying asks so our legal/infra teams can turn around the DPA edits and evidence you requested.

TL;DR: we can support US-only residency, scoped logging evidence, and a limited subprocessor list for the pilot. Need you to confirm a couple items below so we can produce an annotated DPA and a short runbook for your SOC reviewers.

Primary asks
- PII scope: which HealthSync fields do you classify as PII for this pilot? Examples you might confirm: patient name, DOB, MRN, contact email, SSN (we assume SSN is out-of-scope but call it out if you track it).
- Retention windows: pilot goal is short-term evaluation. Do you require retention beyond 30 days for any artifacts (logs, request/response payloads, embeddings)? If yes, specify per-data-class.
- Logging detail: do you need full request/response bodies for audit, or are token-level/metadata logs sufficient (request ID, timestamp, model id, token count, decision reason)?
- Residency: you mentioned US-only — confirm whether that must be enforced at rest only, or both at rest and processing (i.e., inference stay on US-hosted GPUs).
- Subprocessors & notifications: we can provide a limited subprocessor list for the pilot; is advance notice acceptable or do you need prior approval for any subprocessor class (e.g., cloud infra, monitoring)?
- Breach notification window: standard is 72 hours for confirmed incidents. Do you have a shorter SLA requirement?

Attachments: I attached an annotated DPA with inline notes where we typically ask for clarification (redwood-annotated-dpa-draft.pdf). If you can mark the items you want tightened/left as-is, we’ll convert to a narrow-scoped addendum.

Proposed next steps
1) You confirm the PII classes + retention windows (by EOD Thursday if possible).
2) We’ll produce an evidence bundle (logs schema + sample redaction) and submit the annotated DPA to your security contact.
3) If agreed, we’ll circulate a 1-page runbook for breach handling and a short-term subprocessor list for the pilot.

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min sync to run through answers — otherwise reply inline.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-04-11T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: data residency checklist & narrow-scope DPA questions

Thanks Logan — great demo earlier. I’ll respond below to your asks and have our SecurityOps team weigh in on the logging request.

PII scope:
- Confirmed PII for pilot: patient name, DOB, contact email, MRN.
- SSN is not used in the pilot environment.

Retention windows:
- Primary retention: 30 days for request/response payloads.
- Logs (metadata only) retained 180 days.
- Embeddings: HealthSync requests embeddings be purged after 45 days unless we explicitly opt-in to save.

Logging detail:
- SecurityOps prefers metadata logs + hashed payload IDs rather than full plaintext request/response. If you can provide a sample schema, we’ll confirm whether that meets audit needs.

Residency:
- Must be US-only for both storage and processing during the pilot (no cross-border processing).

Subprocessors & notifications:
- Prior notice with 10 business days to object is acceptable for named classes. For any new cloud-region providers, we need prior approval.

Breach notification:
- 48-hour initial notification for suspected confirmed incidents; full incident report within 10 business days.

We attached our security questionnaire for now — SecurityOps will fill the infra questions and return (HSL_security_qs.xlsx).

Eliza
Director, Product Ops
HealthSync Labs

Eliza — perfect, thanks for the clear answers. A few quick clarifications and proposed options so your SecurityOps has concrete artifacts to review:

1) Embeddings purge: we can support an automated purge job at 45 days. We’ll include a config toggle in the pilot to opt-in to longer persistence — default off.

2) Logging schema: attached below is a sample metadata-only log schema we can produce (request_id, timestamp, model_version, token_count, hashed_payload_id, decision_flag). If SecurityOps needs a short sample with redaction markers, we’ll generate that by tomorrow.

3) Residency enforcement: we will pin inference workloads to US-only regions for the pilot and provide an architecture diagram + region ACLs.

4) Subprocessor process: we’ll provide a 10-business-day notification list and will surface any new region providers for approval. For the pilot we propose the following named subprocessors: AWS (us-east-1), Cloud Monitoring Provider (log-ops-us), and our CDP for billing (payment-vendor-us). Please flag any you want us to remove.

Next steps I’ll take on now:
- Produce the redwood evidence bundle + log sample (ETA end of day tomorrow).
- Update the annotated DPA to reflect the 45-day embeddings purge + US-only residency language and circulate to Marissa/legal for a narrow addendum version.
- Share a 1-pager runbook for breach notification with timelines matching your ask (48-hour notice).

If it helps, I can send a short Mutual Action Plan with milestones and a DocuSign link for the pilot addendum acceptance.

Logan

Hi Eliza — looping in from Legal/Privacy. Thanks for the quick answers — confirm we will: 
- Swap the DPA residency clause to a US-only processing and storage carve-out for the pilot.
- Document the 45-day embeddings purge and 30-day request/response retention (logs retained 180 days as metadata).
- Add a 10-business-day notification process for subprocessors and exclude approval for named infra providers unless you flag them.
- Adopt a 48-hour initial breach notification SLA for confirmed incidents and follow with a 10-business-day root cause and remediation report.

I’ll review the annotated DPA Logan attached and produce a pilot addendum that contains only the items we agreed on. Expect a draft by Friday. If there are any non-negotiable security controls in your questionnaire, please flag them separately so I can escalate.

Best,
